sections.title: Nem, is and de
sections.content: Put *nem* before the verb to say you do not like something: *Nem szeretem a sportot. Nem szeretek olvasni.* Ask a friend with the *te* forms. For a known thing the verb is definite: *Szereted a zenét?* For an activity it is indefinite: *Szeretsz olvasni?* The answer repeats the verb: *Igen, szeretem.* or *Igen, szeretek.*

sections.title: Two people, one opinion
sections.content: Use *is* (too) for the same opinion and *de* (but) for a different one: *Anna szereti a zenét, én is.* *A zene érdekel, de a sport nem.* Use *hanem* after a *nem* clause: *Nem a sportot szeretem, hanem a zenét.*

items.spanish: Anna szereti a zenét, én is.
items.english: Anna likes music, and so do I.

items.spanish: A zene érdekel, de a sport nem.
items.english: Music interests me, but sport does not.

sections.content: Look at what follows the verb. After *a* + a noun use *szeretem*. Before an infinitive use *szeretek*. Mixing them (*szeretek a zenét*) is the most common mistake.
